memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction medium. The earnings side is high-conviction on delivered numbers; the return side is a working hypothesis on the multiple. The park rule does not bite: management B, business quality B, predictability C, trackability C, no D or F on the four gates. Entry discipline: the eighteen-month bar (20 percent a year) is cleared at the current price (USD 67.21 on 2026-09-14; CHF 53.76 on 2026-09-22); the three-year bar needs either a price about 9 percent lower (about $61 on the New York line, about CHF 50 on the record's own derivation) or evidence that moves the modal multiple to 20x, which is the implantables re-acceleration. Next-stage work goes to that item first: expert checks on United States premium lens share and PureSee's domestic pricing, and the Unity order funnel beyond Q3 2026. Named conditions that would change the view: a further sector de-rating with Alcon's revisions still positive moves 'Modal return' to D and removes the eighteen-month clearance; implantables growth below zero for two quarters or United States presbyopia-correcting share below 65 percent invalidates the clearing and forces a new sorting; a second actual problem beside implantables (an impairment above $200 million; receivables growing faster than sales for a second year; a guide below consensus) moves 'Riskiness' to D and the case to park.
case: - Alcon is a cause-for-concern-clearing case in an oversold, number-one ophthalmology franchise: core EPS compounding at 12 to 15 percent again on a broad, dated product cycle, and the shares at the lowest multiple of their own five-year range. The earnings alone pay about 11 percent a year while waiting; the case clears the 20 percent bar over eighteen months only if the 24-month-forward multiple recovers from 15.5x to about 18x, and half of that recovery is a call on a sector currently refusing to re-rate.

- The change is internal and it is a product cycle, not a change of people or strategy: Unity VCS and CS consoles (FDA 510(k) June 2024) into a 30,000-unit installed base on a ten-year replacement cycle, equipment +23 and +25 percent constant currency in Q1 and Q2 2026 (the largest equipment beat in three years, over 1,000 qualified leads); PanOptix Pro (April 2025; over 90 percent of domestic PanOptix accounts converted; 50 percent less light scatter; launching in Europe, Japan and Korea in H2 2026); Precision7 (sales more than doubled year on year in Q2 2026) and TOTAL30 Multifocal for Astigmatism; Tryptyr (about 5 percent share within twelve months, 84,000 prescriptions in five months, sell-side $110 million in 2026, $250 to $400 million at peak); Systane multi-dose preservative-free +40 percent; Valeda; 10 to 15 launches over two years. Underneath: a $100 million run-rate cost programme by year-end 2026 (about $50 million in FY2026; $150 million implementation cost) and the $1.5 billion buyback. Internal forces pass the screen's three-strong rule (new products A; guidance raised B; shareholder returns B; standards B; price B); the caveat is that the May raise was share-count driven and about half the August raise ($0.04 of the $0.07 at the midpoint) was the $20 million tariff refund drop-through.

- The external forces do not help and one hurts. Demand grows at low single digits and is not changing pace (global cataract procedures +3 to +5 percent a year; international +3 to +4 percent in Q2 2026; United States flat on surgeon capacity; premium lenses 17 percent of global cataract volumes in 2026 from 12 percent in 2022; United States advanced-technology penetration +180 basis points year on year). Competition tightened at the premium lens edge since late 2024 (Tecnis Odyssey and enVista Envy took United States presbyopia-correcting share from over 80 percent to 66 percent in Q1 2025; PanOptix Pro stabilised it at 70 to 73 percent; PureSee about $150 or 15 percent below Vivity in Europe, 10 to 20 percent share in targeted practices, United States approval March 2026; Bausch + Lomb premium lens revenue +175 percent in Q2 2026; enVista Beyond trial missed its depth-of-focus target). Politics moved from headwind to mixed (IEEPA ruling of 20 February 2026 brings an expected $60 million refund in Q3 2026, $40 million to R&D and $20 million to core operating income; a temporary 10 percent Section 122 tariff; net 2026 tariffs $40 to $90 million; a proposed 12 percent Medicare cataract fee cut; China's second procurement round in 2026 on 5 to 6 percent of sales, management aiming to hold China flat by volume). Currency turned from a drag (over 100 basis points of margin a year 2022 to 2024; $0.15 of EPS in FY2025) to a small tailwind. The supply side is a tailwind to gross margin (largest supplier 5 percent of spend; Lifecore the named single point of failure for hyaluronic acid). The company's own cycle has turned (constant-currency growth 3 percent in Q2 2025, 6 percent Q1 2026, 7 percent Q2 2026). A separate external dynamic pushes against the return: the sector's own de-rating.
counter_case: - At the head of the 'Investment Thesis': the Q2 2026 beat was low quality and the de-rating is right. Equipment placements (+25 percent) are a one-off replacement spike on a ten-year cycle and fade in 2027 against +23 and +25 percent comparisons (and against Q3 2025 +13 percent, Q4 2025 +18 percent); the refund is timing; implantables are trapped at 1 percent because PureSee, enVista Envy and the Light Adjustable Lens (150 to 180 implants a year per high-volume practice) have permanently taken the growth of the category; United States volumes are capped by surgeon capacity and a proposed 12 percent Medicare cataract fee cut; margins are capped near 20 to 21 percent by the Swiss franc cost mismatch, net tariffs of $40 to $90 million, R&D at 9 percent of sales and Aurion's trial costs; earnings growth reverts to the 8 percent post-spin average that Pershing Square itself cites once the launches annualise. European medtech consumables as a group have de-rated to their own lows (eleven of seventeen peers at or below the 5th percentile of their own history with negative revisions; Cooper cutting guidance; Zeiss restructuring), and the market knows something about the group's growth that the bulls do not. On that path core EPS grows 8 to 10 percent a year, the multiple stays at 15x and the return is 9 to 11 percent a year, an F to a D. The evidence for it is real: two quarters of implantables at 1 percent, a 175 percent premium-lens surge at a rival, a whole peer set at its lows, a guidance rise that was about half refund, and a beat that did not move the price. Conceded: the de-rating is partly sector-wide, so half the re-rating is not ours to earn; implantables at 1 percent is the weak link and the re-acceleration is given only about 42 percent (share held at 70 percent or above about 70 percent, implantables at 3 percent or more given that about 60 percent); the August raise was about half refund; if the sector's fair level is 14x the return is 4 to 7 percent a year. The response: the earnings path does not depend on the sector or on implantables growing; consumables (about 24 percent of consensus revenue, +5 percent on the installed base) and contact lenses (record share, +5 percent with four points of price) are the annuity; even with equipment growth at zero in 2027 and implantables flat, group revenue grows 4 to 5 percent and core EPS about 10 percent on margin and share count, about a 10 percent annual return at an unchanged 15.5x, a D and not a loss; the share stabilisation at 70 to 73 percent with over 90 percent account conversion is delivered evidence against permanent share loss and the enVista Beyond miss delays the next challenge; the sell-side's FY2027 range ($3.80 to $4.26) already spans bear and bull and the price sits at the bottom of it; the three tests (equipment below 15 percent constant currency for two consecutive quarters; implantables below zero for two quarters or share below 65 percent; margin expansion below 90 basis points in H2 2026) are measurable within two quarters. Where it wins: a further sector de-rating with Alcon's revisions still positive means the multiple is not ours to earn at all; 'Modal return' to D and the eighteen-month clearance gone.

- At the head of the 'Foundations': the quality is in the core numbers, not in the business. Reported return on invested capital 5 percent; amortisation of purchased intangibles equal to nearly all of five-year adjusted net income; Morgan Stanley ranks reporting quality bottom-tier; inventory provisions and receivables both up about $206 million in 2025; the 2025 miss came from an operator experts describe as pushy enough to lose accounts (grievances 737 to 880; "arm-twisting"). At the premium edge the structure has changed for good: three rivals have launched optics priced or positioned against Alcon since late 2024, and the Light Adjustable Lens is inside Alcon's tent only because Alcon could not build the next optic itself (PowerVision written off for $402 million). On that reading the "high quality" in the pattern is a core-earnings artefact and the "transient" concern is structural. Conceded: the core-to-reported gap is wide and carried; the reported return fails the framework's 15 percent test; share at the premium edge does not compound. Response: free cash flow of $1.70 billion exceeded core net income of about $1,520 million, so the core figure is confirmed in cash and the gap is amortisation of intangibles inherited at the spin, not operating leakage; the installed-base annuity and the contact-lens franchise are the compounding advantages the pattern asks for and neither depends on the premium edge; PanOptix Pro's conversion and the share stabilisation are the disproving evidence against structural inferiority the framework asks for; the operator's answer to 2025 is delivered, not promised. Where it wins: implantables growth negative for two quarters or share below 65 percent makes the concern structural; 'Foundations' to C on the industry Element and the pattern loses its clearing condition.
triggers: - Next-stage work, in order: expert checks on United States premium lens share and PureSee's domestic pricing; the Unity order funnel beyond Q3 2026; both named by the earnings review as its own verification checks.

- Implantables growth and United States premium lens share (Key Driver; the concern that must clear): current +1 percent constant currency (Q2 2026), share 70 to 73 percent; modal +3 percent by 2027 with share held at 70 percent, possible rather than plausible at about 42 percent, skew to the downside; consensus segment revenue $1,474 million to $1,565 million over three years; alarm below 1 percent growth or share below 68 percent; invalidate share below 65 percent (the risks research's trigger) or growth below zero for two quarters. Confirm above 3 percent for three quarters.

- Unity placements and consumables pull-through (Key Driver): equipment +25 percent constant currency (Q2 2026); modal +15 percent in H2 2026 and high single digits in 2027, probable at about 65 percent; guidance double-digit for 2026; consensus segment $898 million to $1,035 million; alarm below 15 percent for one quarter; invalidate below 15 percent for two consecutive quarters (read as the cycle exhausting early).

- Core operating margin (Key Driver): +150 basis points constant currency (Q2 2026); modal +150 in 2026 then +90 to +100 a year, 22.2 percent FY2027 and 23.0 percent FY2028, probable at about 60 percent; guidance +90 to +190 basis points for 2026; consensus EBITDA margin 26.3 to 28.2 percent (brokers' basis); alarm below 90 basis points; invalidate a year of contraction; confirm 150 basis points or more in Q3 and Q4 2026; a 2027 guide below +50 basis points changes the view.
- Core EPS: H1 2026 $1.69; modal $3.50, $3.95, $4.45; guidance $3.45 to $3.55 (or $3.49 to $3.58); consensus $3.49, $3.91, $4.48; alarm a guide below consensus; invalidate a cut.

- The multiple: 15.41x (2026-09-11); modal 18x in eighteen months; branch odds about 35 percent at 15.5x, 40 percent at 18x, 25 percent at 21x; alarm below 14x (crash band); no invalidate level, a lower multiple with unchanged earnings is an entry question. A further sector de-rating with Alcon's revisions still positive moves the modal branch to no re-rating and 'Modal return' to D.
